estimate 3, component web, phase "P3 Drawing & Alerts", perspective Product, risk "R5 Scope", parent E27, milestone
"R3 Trading on demo" (`E27.json:371-391`); due 2026-12-24 (`31:2672`). `blocked_by` **E27-D02 — merged** as text
(#4338, `bf130fe52`); its boards are PENDING and the owner's `approved` on #733 is pending, and this spec builds on
the merged text (BQ-1). **Blocks** E27-D04 (motion), E27-D05 (the a11y review) and E27-D06 (the handoff pack)
(`31:2641-2643`); the first consumer, E27-S01, starts in Sprint 15 (`D02:49`).

stands in for the Chief Design Officer's and the Security engineer's sign-offs; agent-delivery adaptations, owner
decision 2026-09-25). Every decision is **PROPOSED** unless marked **RULED** with its source. BQ-1…BQ-16
are **RULED** (main-orchestrator, 2026-10-24 14:22Z, [LANE-hcl49]): all sixteen defaults, with BQ-8 bound
now by C-2.7 and C-12.2, BQ-14 amended and BQ-11's props consumed by name; the riders of BQ-5 and BQ-6 and the
supersession of E05-D02's time-limited reveal stay the owner's, PROPOSED. This spec's hi-fi decisions HD1…HD17 (§1)
are PROPOSED. Boards **PENDING** (§0): ten under the lever-4 cap, drawn in the boards PR; no board exists and no

**Method:** a desk spec on merged inputs, with a heuristic evaluation `(heuristic)`; no participant, session, timing
or quote exists, and none is invented. Contrast, greyscale and colour vision are computed by
`docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py` (`python3 -I -B`): every number in this spec is its output, `--check`
re-derives every `<!-- audit:… -->` marker, and `--self-test` refuses its mutation set on its fixture and on this
spec, and the standing rule's K list frame row by frame row (§16). The ticket's "contrast measured with the design-system plugin" is
that tool; "copy re-tested with two people" is §12.4's heuristic re-test plus a written protocol for the owner and
§15's walkthrough. Nothing was fetched.

**Scope (the ticket):** hi-fi for every state of E27-D02's inventory (§0, §2–§8), in dark and light, with the
densities specified (BQ-3, BQ-4); the contributions CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-176 AccountKeyRow and CMP-034
MaskedValue, and the documented extensions of CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-044, CMP-066 and CMP-178 (§2); the final copy
deck (§12); the Storybook story lists (§13). **Out of scope:** motion (E27-D04) · the a11y audit of the built screens
(E27-D05) · the handoff pack (E27-D06) · design QA (E27-D07) · implementation.

## 0. The boards (PENDING; ten under the lever-4 cap)

Page **`E27-D03 Accounts and key vault hi-fi`** (36 characters), created by name by the board script at the boards
step and its id recorded then (`docs/design/README.md:46-49`). Boards are `E27-D03 / NN slug`; the frames nested in
them keep E27-D02's names (`SCR-nnn / <state>`), so §0, the hi-fi rows of §2–§8 and `D02:911-1009` reconcile
mechanically. Exports go to `docs/design/E27/img/E27-D03-NN-<slug>.png` at 1:1 through
`docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`, with `-greyscale`, `-deuteranopia` and `-protanopia` renders for boards 01 and
02 (`docs/design/_tools/cvd_sim.py`; BQ-16). Every PROPOSED decision carries its stamp; "not yet served — {gap},
{owner}" strips sit on a board annotation layer, never product UI and never a story (`D02:57-58`, `D02:326-331`);
fixture values only; every time in UTC. **Every board is PENDING; no export is claimed.**

**PROPOSED deviation (the lever-4 board cap: main-orchestrator, 2026-10-24 03:11Z, [LANE-hcl39]).** The ruling,
quoted: "the lever-4 board cap applies to every not-yet-drawn set, old specs included: **≤ 10 boards per ticket, light
twins ≤ one third**, chosen for the evidence that matters (the T2 / safety / contrast / state-matrix boards; one
anatomy; one keyboard-a11y; the redline of the one contract-bearing screen); every other sheet is listed in §0 as
"not drawn — the text is binding; drawn on request", which the owner's text-first lever already allows." AC1's
"every state … in dark and light" is therefore met in text: every one of E27-D02's 78 frames has a hi-fi row with
its light binding by token (§2–§8), ten composite boards draw the evidence, two of them light twins of the
contrast-critical boards (BQ-2), and high contrast is proven by the computed matrix (§9; the E42-D03 Q6 precedent,
`E42-D03:152`). The board choice follows the ruling's order and its tie-breaker (contrast-critical screens, the DEMO
/ LIVE badge, the two disabled looks), and E27-D02's own guidance (main-orchestrator, 2026-10-24 07:35Z): the key

**Not drawn — the text is binding; drawn on request:** SCR-019's three frames
(`SCR-019 / account task pending`; `SCR-019 / account task done`; `SCR-019 / account task blocked with reason`),
content-only rows in §8 because their CMP-097 chrome is E09's (BQ-1); the light twins of boards 03 and 06–10; every
high-contrast board (high contrast is proven by §9's matrix, BQ-3); per-state sheets; SCR-079's comfortable frames
beyond board 09's inset (BQ-4). Each is binding as text in its section, and its hi-fi row's Board cell says so.

**Build order** (the boards PR, after the ruling): 01, 03, 04, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, then the twins 02 and 05. The
script runs through `docs/design/_tools/penpot_exec.py`, finds the page by name, stamps every board with "page
E27-D03 · board NN · rN" and is posted on the PR with its sha256; the page is referenced by name and id only (R7).

**Reconciliation.** The audit tool checks that every frame a board lists has its hi-fi row naming that board, that
every other frame's row says "not drawn — the text is binding; drawn on request", that no frame sits on two boards
(a twin lists none of its own), and that a `drawn` row has its board id, its PNG and, for boards 01 and 02, its
three renders.

## 2. Design-system contributions

### 2.1 CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge — the variant set (AC2, AC3)

Built to BQ-5 and BQ-6, their riders PROPOSED for the owner. This spec owns CMP-175's E27 state set and its visual
vocabulary, which amends OQ-12 (`MEMO:528-533`); E43-D02 (#1139) extends it additively — Bybit provenance on the
verdict, drift naming, SCR-128's hardening — and its `VerificationVerdict` names map one to one: `verified-off` is
`verified`, `verified-on` is `detected`, `unverifiable` is `not_checked` and `stale` is `overdue` (`E43.json:97`;
D03-H4, §14). One component, never a parallel badge: every withdrawal, rights and allowlist verdict word in E27 is a
CMP-175 word, and so is Bybit's own expiry, while the rotation policy's clock stays CMP-011's (D7, `D02:193`). The table
is the variant set the audit tool gates (§16): one row per state — the ticket's eight (its CMP-175 deliverable), read-only's import and
stored forms apart, plus "not checked", "check overdue" and the allowlist facet's pass and unread forms.

**Reading the table.** The word carries each state and is its own (AC2); the glyph repeats the class — check pass,
octagon failed and critical, triangle warning, clock time warning, dash not checked, info a stored read-only key, and
the lock is T2's alone — and no warning-class state ever takes the octagon (BQ-6; `D02:235`, `D02:634`). `icon/check`,
`icon/minus` and `icon/info` are the registry's names; `icon/octagon`, `icon/triangle` and `icon/clock` are DS-5's
(`E42-D02:1006`), and where the registry's own warning and danger glyphs already draw the triangle and the octagon, the
registry's name serves (E05-T06's registry decides; E10-D03 C23): the shape is the carrier, never the name. Variants of
one class share its glyph and differ by their words: a glyph per variant would need invented shapes and would break one
shape per class (BQ-6). The ✓ in the verified word is that check glyph, `aria-hidden` beside the words. "OFF" appears in
the verified word only and always with its time (AD-3); a key whose rights were never read reads "Withdrawal: not
checked" (`22:16950`, `22:16988-16990`).

**AC2 — greyscale and colour vision.** Colour reinforces and never carries (BQ-6): each variant differs from every other
by its word, from every other class by its glyph's shape, and the critical variant from the failed ones by its weight,
its border and its first word — all of them shape and text, so all of them survive greyscale and every simulation. The
fills cannot carry it, as §9 measures: under deuteranopia the critical and pass fills sit ΔE76
4.46 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-critical-pass.dark.deuteranopia=4.46 --> apart in dark and
1.05 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-critical-pass.light.deuteranopia=1.05 --> in light, under the 5.0 JND; the octagon's and the
triangle's strong tokens are one colour in light, ΔE76 0.00 <!-- audit:cvd.glyph-critical-warning.light.normal=0.0 -->
in every simulation (DS-6, `E42-D02:1007`); and in greyscale the danger and warning fills are Rec. 601 luma
38 <!-- audit:luma.color.status.danger.subtle.dark=38 --> and 52 <!-- audit:luma.color.status.warning.subtle.dark=52 -->
in dark, 233 <!-- audit:luma.color.status.danger.subtle.light=233 --> and
238 <!-- audit:luma.color.status.warning.subtle.light=238 --> in light. Boards 01 and 02 draw the set with its
greyscale, deuteranopia and protanopia renders (BQ-16); §9 reports every pair's ΔE76 and luma, never gated.

**AC3 — withdrawal-detected reads as blocking.** Beside the ordinary warnings — rotation due, Bybit expiry and degraded
on the triangle, check overdue and rotation overdue on the clock (`D02:389-392`, `D02:415`, `D02:634-635`) — the
critical state is the octagon; beside the failed states, which share the octagon, it alone is a bold word inside a 2 px
border, and its word leads with "BLOCKED"; bold is reserved for critical states (`16:85`). Its row adds the danger
treatment (§2.2), the page the server's read-only banner and the negated verdict (`D02:403-410`), and its first control
starts the compromise response, never Rotate (OQ-13; `keys.compromise_path`, `D02:316`). The border measures
9.32 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-critical-border.dark=9.32 --> / 4.11 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-critical-border.light=4.11 --> /
9.32 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-critical-border.high-contrast=9.32 --> against the row (§9 `c175-critical-border`) and the
word on its fill 12.06 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-danger-word.dark=12.06 --> /
14.64 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-danger-word.light=14.64 --> /
13.66 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-danger-word.high-contrast=13.66 --> (`c175-danger-word`). No fresh reviewer exists, so AC3
is checked by heuristic and an owner-walkthrough item (§15); none is invented.

**OWNER-LEVEL rider (BQ-6): no solid red, no local hue.** Whether `color.status.*` gains a distinct critical hue is the
owner's decision A6 (`16:54`), or DS-6's for the palette owner (`E42-D02:1007`); this spec neither adopts DS-6's red nor
overrides a colour locally (the ticket's Technical notes), and re-raises DS-6 with §9's evidence. A solid
`color.status.danger.default` chip is rejected: its label measures
4.54 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-solid-danger.high-contrast=4.54 --> in high contrast, under the 7.0 hc-text bar (§9
`c175-solid-danger`), and in high contrast its fill sits ΔE76
2.56 <!-- audit:cvd.solid-danger-live.high-contrast.protanopia=2.56 --> from the LIVE accent under protanopia and
3.83 <!-- audit:cvd.solid-danger-live.high-contrast.deuteranopia=3.83 --> under deuteranopia (`solid-danger-live`),
where `16:57` keeps `color.env.live` unambiguous.

#### CMP-175: scopes, forms and the aggregate line

- **`key` scope** — one facet of one key: withdrawal, rights, allowlist or expiry. Two forms: `badge` (fill, glyph and
  word: CMP-176's state slot, and the critical state everywhere) and `inline` (glyph and word on the host's surface:
  CMP-176's facet cells, SCR-128's table cells and SCR-079's key block). The critical state is never the `inline` form:
  a host that lists the facets inline shows it as the badge, SCR-079's statement list included (§8). Under a header
  that names the facet — CMP-176's line 2 under "IP allowlist", SCR-128's Allowlist column — an allowlist word drops
  its "IP allowlist: " lead ("matches", "no match", "none set", "not checked"); everywhere else the word is whole.
  No expiry, or one beyond 14 days, draws no expiry facet; the drawer's key line then states the date or "Bybit expiry:
  none" as plain metadata (`D02:784`).
- **`aggregate` scope** — the withdrawal verdict line under SCR-125's `h1` (D3; `D02:212-230`): one line, never
  dismissible, its words the carrier. It reads the server's notices and computes no verdict of its own; its time is the
  oldest `last_verified_at` until G-2 serves one (O-B, `D02:1212`). No fill; the system banner above the band (CMP-092)
  carries the server's own sentence (`D02:229-230`).

#### CMP-175: accessibility and keyboard

- Static text: not focusable. The word is its text; the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"` beside it; its host's table cell
  gives it a header.
- The critical word leads with "BLOCKED" and is read first; it is the only bold state word in its row. A LIVE row's
  CMP-075 pill is bold too (§3.1 block I), so weight is never the row's carrier there: the octagon, the 2 px border,
  the danger fill, the 4 px rule and the first control are (§2.2, §3.2).
- No live region of its own: its host announces a transition once through the shell announcer — a failed key assertive,
  a recovery polite (D21; `D02:1078-1079`) — and the aggregate line per the forms table.
- No keyboard of its own: the actions are its row's (§2.2).
- Forced colours: the fills drop; the word and the glyph are `CanvasText`; the critical 2 px border is `CanvasText` — a
  border, so the critical state stays apart (BQ-3).

### 2.3 CMP-034 MaskedValue — permanently masked (AC4)

Binding now: C-2.7 keeps plaintext inside the secrets module, and C-12.2 lets a response carry only key metadata —
label, masked id, permissions, environment (`CON:136-140`, `CON:747-757`; `SECR:15`; main-orchestrator ruling,
2026-10-24 14:22Z, [LANE-hcl49], on BQ-8). Only the supersession of E05-D02's time-limited display of client-held values
stays the owner's, as a C-row and a copy-ready A-row to E05-D02's owner, PROPOSED (D03-C4, D03-A3; §14); no board draws one meanwhile.
**Gap:** the entry (`15:371-379`, E05-D02's respec) defines a toggle, a timer and a copy control that AC4, US-ACCT-002
and C-2.7 forbid, and its name promises what no screen may offer.

| Sizes     | the box's `size.control.height` and `space.inset.sm` (`15:377`)                                                                                             | none of its own: text in its host's line, alike in both densities (density never changes type, `16:125`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

**The description** is the deck's `e27.cmp034.description` (§12.1), PROPOSED: "Shows the last 4 characters of the
key ID only. The full key and its secret are write-only and can't be shown anywhere in CandleViewer." One node per
page holds it, in the DOM at mount, and every CMP-034 on the page points at it by `aria-describedby` (one node, many
pointers), so a page that names several keys carries it once; a screen reader meets it with a key id, and it never
names a control. The accessible name is `e27.cmp034.name`, "API key, ending in a1b2" in frame 6.

**Why the reveal is deliberately absent** (the rationale the entry records, AC4). There is nothing to show and nowhere
it could come from. C-2.7 keeps every secret and decrypted key out of any API response, WS frame and frontend bundle,
the secrets module exposing signing and metadata reads only (`CON:136-140`); C-12.2 and `SECR:15` let a response carry
only key metadata; `listApiKeys` returns "metadata only" and `key_id_masked` holds at most the last 4 characters, the
rest never stored in clear (`22:2677-2678`, `22:16879-16882`; KV-I07, `TM:256`); and US-ACCT-002 asks for "no reveal
control anywhere in the app or API" (`11:344`). A reveal path is a threat in itself — KV-I06 (`TM:255`), SR-E27-11
(`TM:664`), probes recorded as `api_key.reveal_attempt` (`ACT:139`) — and E27-D02's D13 and the memo's AD-11 bind it
(`D02:199`, `MEMO:407`). The ticket names "a masked value that implies a reveal is available" among the
misrepresentations that cause a wrong decision (its Security notes): a box, a toggle, a timer or a copy control on a
masked id would imply exactly that, so all four are gone, and the old name stays only as an annotated historical name.

**What it supersedes.** E05-D02 respecified CMP-034 (#4322) as a time-limited display of a value the client holds in the
current flow on SCR-126 and SCR-127 (rules S1–S7, `E05F:748-795`), flagged to the security engineer for E05-X02 (G19,
`E05F:448-453`). Under BQ-8 nothing on those screens displays a client-held secret: entry is CMP-201's write-only
variant (below) and a stored key is CMP-034's masked id. S4–S7 — nothing leaks, copy never logs, only a value the client
holds, short-lived — move to that variant; S1–S3 and G20 (`E05F:454-456`) lapse with the display. The supersession is
the owner's (D03-C4).

Documented, not forked (the ticket's extensions deliverable; AC6): each entry gains a variant or props, never a sibling component. The exact edits are
Appendix A's. CMP-044 and CMP-178 carry E42-D03's unlanded proposals on the same lines (`E42-D03:892-896`,
`E42-D03:902-904`): their props are consumed here by name, PROPOSED with a "contract pending" stamp until they land, so
this spec never depends on an unmerged PR (the ruling on BQ-11); if E42-D03's boards PR (`design/e42-d03-boards`) lands
its Appendix A first, re-read and re-base (GATE R6, `GATE:79-80`). CMP-066 is the same case with E42-D05
(`E42-D05:921-922`): its unlanded status set is consumed by name, PROPOSED, contract pending, and whichever lands
second re-bases.

#### CMP-028 — the KEK-unavailable notice (BQ-9; frames 17, 29, 41 and 45)

- **Anatomy.** The octagon (`icon/octagon`) · sentence 1, "Off while the credential key is unavailable.", which is the
  `keys.kek_unavailable` string and the node every blocked key control's `aria-describedby` points at · sentence 2,
  "Keys can't be added, tested or rotated until the KEK is back, and trading is off." (`D02:418-419`, `D02:1117`).
- **Where.** One per screen under its `h1` — SCR-125, SCR-126 and once in SCR-128's panel — beside the server's banner
  (D17, `D02:203`); on SCR-127 the wizard does not open and Rotate key… points at SCR-125's notice (`D02:585`).
- **The global banner is CMP-092, consumed.** Its blocking row carries the server's sentence, "Trading disabled: the
  credential key is unavailable." (`SYS:66`), and is the one announcement for the condition (`15:935`); the panel notice
  is CMP-028's `blocking` form and announces nothing.

  revoke.
- **States.** One: present while `secrets.kek_unavailable` holds (`23:4262`), gone when it clears.

#### CMP-035 — the 900 s rotation overlap (BQ-10; frame 38)

- **Where.** SCR-127 stage 4 only: "Switched at 10:40:01 UTC. New requests use ...d9e0. The old key ...e5f6 keeps
  working here until 10:55:01 UTC — 14:12 left — while requests in flight finish. Open orders stay open."
  (`D02:575-577`). CMP-035 renders "until 10:55:01 UTC — 14:12 left".
- **Times.** The served `overlap_until` (`22:17133`) is the primary, absolute time; the 900 s is fixed and no request
  changes it (`22:2885-2889`). The time left is secondary and counts on server-corrected time (`serverOffsetMs`), never
  a claim of the client's clock.
- **Stage changes.** The stage moves on the server's `state`, `overlapping` to `completed` (`22:17134`), never on the
  countdown reaching 0; at 0 it reads "0:00 left" and waits (DJ).
- **Announcements.** `aria-live="off"`; polite at 60 s and 10 s, each with the absolute time — the deck's
  `e27.scr127.overlap.at60` and `.at10` (§12.1), "1 minute left on the old key ...e5f6, until 10:55:01 UTC." and "10
  seconds left on the old key ...e5f6, until 10:55:01 UTC." — and the end is CP-4's `e27.scr127.stage5.revoked`,
  polite once, with focus on stage 5's heading if the wizard is open (`D02:586-588`; D21, `D02:207`).
- **Colour.** None under a threshold (`warnBelowS: null`): the end of the overlap is the expected path, not a fault, and
  the warning text name is no token (`15:386`).
- **The row.** Only the absolute line, "Rotation in progress · old key usable until 10:55:01 UTC" (`D02:578`), nothing
  ticking in a list (D21).
- **`Esc`** at stage 4 closes the view; the server's overlap continues (`D02:588-589`).
- **Tokens.** Both times `type.num.base`; the absolute `color.text.primary`,
  13.27 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-text.dark=13.27 --> / 14.37 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-text.light=14.37 --> /
  15.02 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-text.high-contrast=15.02 --> (`dialog-text`); the time left `color.text.secondary`,
  8.14 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-secondary.dark=8.14 --> / 8.26 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-secondary.light=8.26 --> /
  13.27 <!-- audit:pairs.dialog-secondary.high-contrast=13.27 --> (`dialog-secondary`).
- **Sizes.** Text inside its sentence, alike in both densities.

## 3. SCR-125 — Bybit accounts list (`/admin/accounts`; boards 04 and 05)

Hi-fi of E27-D02 §5.1 (`D02:338-438`) inside the CMP-087 shell as E42-D03 §4 draws it (`E42-D03:163-205`),
consumed and never redrawn. Board 04 nests every frame of §3.4 at 1280 × 800 in dark, with §3.1's anatomy redline
first; board 05 is its light twin in `semantic-light` (§0, BQ-2). These rules hold for every row of this section and of
§4:

- **Density.** Comfortable only (BQ-4; `16:114`, rule 3 at `16:127`; `D02:132-135`): 32 px rows and controls
  (`size.row.comfortable`, `size.control.comfortable`), the comfortable step `space.3` (12 px) and the
  `space.inset.lg` (16 px) page padding (`16:111-114`; `E42-D02:120`). Rows take `min-height`, so the 150 % text
  scale grows them and never clips (`16:138`). The compact CMP-176 row is §2.2's component specimen, never a third set
  of admin frames (BQ-4).
- **Strings.** Each row names its §12 keys. Where a row quotes text, the text is E27-D02's at the cited line, and
  §12's keyed string wins wherever BQ-15 refines it.
- **Tokens.** Each element's token is named once. Light resolves the same names through `semantic-light`
  (`themes.json` layers it over dark), so a row names a light binding only where one moves. Every pair is measured in
  §9 under the id given here, in dark, light and high contrast. Two light facts recur: `color.status.danger.strong`
  and `color.status.warning.strong` are one colour in light, so the octagon, the triangle and their words carry the
  difference (BQ-6); and the status glyphs on their fills and on the row read lowest in light, still above the 3.0
  non-text bar (§9: `c175-pass-glyph`, `c175-danger-glyph`, `c175-warning-glyph`, `row-pass-glyph`).
- **Gated controls.** Admin controls carry state legs only, because a non-owner and a view-as session get SCR-155
  (`D02:169-171`, `D02:1013-1014`); no frame here draws a role variant or `rbac.view_as`. A row that draws a gated
  control cites §10.1.
- **Stamps and fixtures.** A frame that draws a PROPOSED decision carries its stamp, and a target state its "not yet
  served — {gap}, {owner}" strip, on the board's annotation layer, never as product UI or a story (BQ-2;
  `D02:57-58`, `D02:326-331`). Fixture values only (the Key); every time in UTC.

**Focus and keys (R3).** Skip link → TopBar → NavRail → strip items → "+ Add account" → [Change] → per record, in
order: [Start the compromise response] where the record is blocked, then Actions, then Details → the "Key health and
secrets policy" button → RightRail → StatusBar (`D02:434-435`; `E42-D03:199-200`, `E42-D03:589`). The skip link lands
on the `h1`; the band, the verdict line, the region headings and the footer marker hold no control. The table is plain,
not a grid (D22; `D02:208`, `D02:435-436`): its Tab stops are each record's buttons, and its header rows hold none.
`15` turns a table with an interactive body column into a grid (`15:528-530`) while D22 keeps six records or fewer a
plain table, so the conflict goes to `15`'s owner as D03-C5 (§14). `Enter`, `Space` or `↓` on Actions opens the menu,
`↑` / `↓` move, `Enter` picks, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the button. The focus ring is CMP-039's
`color.focus.ring`, 2 px with its offset, so both of its neighbours are the surface it sits on: the page (`ring-page`),
a record (`ring-row`), the blocked record's danger fill (`ring-danger`), the menu and the Test dialog (`ring-dialog`).

### 3.5 The LIVE and DEMO groups

- **Order.** LIVE then DEMO; Main, then its subs by label; the order is stable, so a failure never moves a record, and
  the strip, the verdict and the chip point at it instead (D2; `D02:188`, `D02:371-373`).
- **Carriers.** Each group opens with its `h3` row and count (block I). The environment is text on every record (the
  CMP-075 pill in cell 1) and follows the label wherever it leaves its group: "Actions for sub_001 · LIVE", the Test
  dialog's title, strip items and the notices under the `h1` (`D02:262-270`). The word, its weight and the dot's
  shape carry LIVE and DEMO in greyscale and under colour-vision loss; the hue sits only on the 1 px border and the
  dot (`E30-D04:173-176`; §9 `env-live`, `env-demo`).
- **One environment.** A deployment that serves one environment shows that one group and names it (OQ-4, PROPOSED;
  `D02:497-498`); the capacity line counts the process environment's subs (`22:21771-21806`). Frame 6 draws both
  groups, as E27-D02 does.
- **No exemption.** The allowlist check, the verdict and every chip apply to demo-1 as to the LIVE accounts
  (`22:2722-2726`; AD-4 at `MEMO:400`).

### 3.6 Zoom, text scale, forced colours and announcements (R1, R2; §11 holds the set)

- **125 %** on 1280 × 800 (1024 CSS px): the content is 720 px, 688 inside, and the four columns keep their shares
  (25 · 25 · 29 · 20 %); cells wrap, records grow, no column is dropped (BQ-4).
- **200 %:** one card per account, the label line first, then the two-word facts as label–value pairs, Actions after
  the label (`D02:1087-1088`); the Test dialog fills the viewport, its body scrolls and its Cancel and Run test row
  stays one sticky row (`D02:1088-1089`).
- **150 % text scale:** records are `min-height` (`16:138`), so a record grows by whole lines; the header rows stay
  sticky.
- **Forced colours (BQ-3):** fills drop, and the chip's word and glyph carry; the critical chip's 2 px border and the
  blocked record's 4 px rule are borders, so they survive as `CanvasText`; a gated item's label and lock render
  `GrayText` and its reason `CanvasText`; the focus ring renders `Highlight` (`E42-D03:642`).
- **Announcements (D21; `D02:1076-1083`):** the verdict line silently, since CMP-092's row speaks for every negated
  form's condition (`15:935`; D03-C9); a health transition once through the shell announcer; the Test result assertive on a refusal
  and polite on a pass; a keystroke on a gated item polite, its reason; CMP-092's blocking row its own single
  announcement (`15:935`).

## 4. SCR-126 — Add or edit a Bybit account, and SCR-016 step 3 (board 06)

Hi-fi of E27-D02 §5.2 (`D02:440-536`) and of SCR-016's account step (§5.7, `D02:847-873`). Board 06 nests frames
18–32 at 1280 × 800 in dark, with §4.1's redline first, and SCR-016's four frames as insets (BQ-1); light is bound by
token and not drawn (§0: board 06 has no twin; the text is binding). Both screens are comfortable (BQ-4; `16:114`);
§3's rules for strings, tokens, gated controls, stamps and fixtures hold here. One "Verify and save" verifies and
stores in one call: there is no test before saving, and the button never waits on one (D5; `D02:463-466`; `22:2696`).

**Focus and keys (R3).** Skip link → strip → the stepper's done step → Copy → API key → API secret → Cancel → Verify
and save (`D02:532-533`). `Enter` in a field sends the step's one action. After an answer focus moves to the result
heading; then the summary's controls, then the form card's stops again, so a refused key is fixed and verified again
without going back (`D02:533-534`). The ring on a field sits against the card (`ring-row`) and its well (`ring-page`).
At 200 % the form and result cards take the full width and the stepper collapses to its current step; at the 150 %
text scale the wells keep `min-height` and the help lines wrap (R1; `16:138`).

**Budget** ≤ 3 s for the round trip inside the 12 s server hold (`14:2539`; `ADR9:214-215`), with the validating state
(D18). **Events:** `accounts.create` (`ACT:134`) and `api_key.import` (`ACT:136`) on a pass, `security.key_policy_violation`
on a refusal (`ACT:147`), `api_key.import` then `api_key.revoke` on a failed activation (`ACT:138`), `account.updated`
with no registered code (a marker without one), `admin.key_form_opened` (analytics, PROPOSED) (`D02:475-478`).

### 4.4 SCR-016 step 3 — the account step as insets (board 06)

The step is SCR-126 inline (`14:417`; `D02:864-866`): one "Verify and save" registers the shell and verifies and
stores the key (D5); the verdict is a row the server fills after a pass, never a box the owner ticks (C-7; the memo's
F-19, `MEMO:260`); the environment is the deployment's, stated in words (OQ-4). The four frames are insets on board 06 at 1280 ×
800, comfortable (BQ-4). The wizard's chrome around the step, its six-step CMP-066 `nav` stepper and its Back · Skip for
now · Continue row, is drawn as E27-D02 §5.7 lays it out (`D02:849-861`); the steps beyond 3 and the completion state
are the onboarding owner's (`D02:1165-1167`).

## 5. SCR-127 — Key rotation (board 07)

A modal wizard, opened by "Rotate key…" from SCR-125's row menu, SCR-128's per-key menu or SCR-126's edit key row
(`D02:421-422`, `D02:624`, `D02:520-524`). It runs the contract's two-phase `rotateApiKey` (`22:2876-2950`): the new
key goes through the `createApiKey` pipeline; on a pass the old key turns `rotating`, both keys work for the fixed
900 s overlap while requests in flight drain, and the old key is then revoked here; no request changes the overlap,
and a suspected compromise never rotates (`22:2885-2893`). The five stages are binding (D8, `D02:194`); their form,
rung 1 with the `keys` step-up (`D02:279`; OQ-10, `MEMO:541`; `SU:522`) and every string here are PROPOSED.
Comfortable density only (BQ-4). Board 07 draws frames 33–41 in dark; light is the same layout by token (no twin,
BQ-2), and the light differences that matter are named per row. No frame draws a rollback, an early revoke, a drain
read, a `failed` state or a schedule control (G-4; AD-6, `MEMO:402`; `D02:582-584`), and no frame shows more of a key
than its masked id `...{last4}` or anything of a secret (BQ-8; C-2.7, C-12.2). Admin is T3 for a Manager, a Viewer
and a view-as session, who meet SCR-155, so this screen's only T2 is a state leg (`D02:1013-1014`).

**Data and producers.** `rotateApiKey`'s `200` is an `ApiKeyRotation` (`new_key`, `verification`, `overlap_until`,
`state: overlapping`; `22:17126-17134`) and drives stages 3 → 4; a `422` is a refusal carrying the `verification` the
pipeline reached, its `egress_ip` included (frame 36; `22:2745-2749`); a `503` is no verdict (frame 37); stage 5 reads
the old key's `revoked` from `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys` (`D02:559-561`). The route is `keys:manage`,
the Owner's alone, and not mounted at the base (`MX:596-602`). The budget is ≤ 10 s across stages 2–3 with each
stage's elapsed time, never the overlap (`14:2552`; C-3, `D02:1198`). Events: `api_key.rotate` once the switch
happens (`ACT:137`), `security.key_policy_violation` on a refused new key, nothing for the instructions or a no-verdict
answer (`D02:954-962`). Not served, and drawn only as frame 40's annotation (D20): a read of requests still in
flight, a rollback, an early revoke and the meaning of `state: failed` (`22:17134`; G-4, #897).

**Keyboard and focus (every frame).** The dialog opens on the stage heading, and every stage change moves focus to the
new heading, which reads it (`D02:587-588`; E42-D05:140). Tab: the stage's controls in DOM order → Cancel or Close →
Back → the primary (`D02:588`). `Esc` is Cancel at stages 1, 2 and 5 and closes the view at 3 and 4, where the
server's rotation goes on (`D02:588-589`). `Enter` acts on Next and on Verify and switch; `Space` toggles the stage-5
note (`D02:1067`); `Enter` in a key field never presses Verify and switch (PROPOSED: a rung's confirm is pressed on
itself, as E42-D03:594 rules for its typed fields). The countdown speaks only at 60 s, 10 s and the end, politely
(D21, `D02:207`); a refusal is assertive once (CMP-027; `D02:590`). On close focus returns to the control that
opened the wizard (`05:97`). At 200 % zoom the dialog fills the viewport, its body scrolls, its footer stays one
sticky row and the stepper collapses to "Stage 2 of 5 — Paste and confirm", there and on any narrow width, with a
disclosure listing the five stages (`D02:1088-1089`; E42-D05:921); at the 150 % text scale controls keep
`min-height` (`16:138`). In forced colours the stepper's glyphs take `currentColor` and its current item
`Highlight` / `HighlightText`, the destructive confirm keeps its 1 px border, and every fill drops while the words
carry (E42-D05:226-228).

**CMP-066 and CMP-035 as used here (BQ-12, BQ-10; the entries' edits are §2.4's and Appendix A's).** CMP-066: the list
form; the statuses by E42-D05's names, glyph and word together; `meta` for the elapsed time — stage 3's request time,
counted in whole seconds while it runs ("Verify · 2 s") and shown to a tenth once it answers ("Verify · 2.4 s"),
measured from the real request and never simulated (D18; AD-16, `MEMO:412`); the collapsed label at 200 %; focus to
the stage heading. CMP-035: `overlap_until` is the primary, absolute time and the relative mm:ss the secondary; it is
text, `type.num.*` replacing `font.mono` (not a token, `15:386`); no warning colour (`color.text.warning` is not a
token either) and no "secret auto-hide" use (BQ-8); the list rows never tick — they show only the absolute line
(`D02:578`).

## 6. SCR-128 — Key health and secrets policy (boards 04 and 05)

A panel of `/admin/accounts` under SCR-125's list, never a route of its own: a CMP-051 disclosure whose header is the
`h2`'s button "Key health and secrets policy" (`aria-expanded`), collapsed by default, its open state kept in the URL
so a strip item can deep-link to it (`D02:622-625`). It holds the rate line, the per-key table, the Test sentence and
the secrets-at-rest policy in sentences; "Suspected compromise…" opens the ordered card first under the `h1`
(`D02:640-645`). Owner only (`audit:read`, `keys:read`; everyone else meets SCR-155, T3); comfortable density on the
screen (BQ-4). Board 04 draws frames 42–48 in dark beside SCR-125's frames and board 05 is its light twin (BQ-2).

**The boundary with E43-D02 (BQ-1).** This section specifies SCR-128's base states, frames 42–48, and nothing else.
E43-D02 (#1139; `E43.json:97`) keeps the hardening states: the verified-against-Bybit provenance and time on the
verdict, drift naming, the KEK id and last re-wrap, the failure counts, the per-UID rate budget and SCR-136. None of
them is drawn here as data — they have no source today (O-H, `D02:1218`), and the policy's runbook sentence stands
for the KEK. The table's rights and allowlist cells are CMP-175's E27 state set (§2.1), which E43-D02 extends
additively and never forks (BQ-5).

At 1280 × 800 the Rights cell's dated word already takes two lines, so a key row is about 44 px (`min-height`). At
125 % zoom on 1280 × 800 (a 1024 CSS px viewport) every column stays: the Rotation due, Rights and Allowlist
cells wrap onto a second line inside `min-height` rows, nothing truncates, no column hides and nothing scrolls
sideways; the same table in compact density (24 px rows, `size.row.compact`) is the component specimen that meets the
ticket's "compact legible at 125 %" clause, drawn with board 10's 125 % specimens (BQ-4). At 200 % the rows reflow to
one card per key, the account and key first, then the facts as label–value pairs, Actions after the key (SCR-125's
reflow, `D02:1087-1088`).

**Data and producers (Owner only).** The table: `GET /admin/security/summary` (`getSecuritySummary`, `audit:read`;
per key `status`, `age_days`, `expires_at`, `withdrawal_permission_present`, `ip_whitelist_matches_expected`,
`last_verified_at`; `22:13742-13754`, `22:22011-22033`; not mounted, `MX:202-208`) and the key list,
`GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys` (`rotation_due_at`, `rotation_state`; `22:16873-16900`), computed
server-side and cached 60 s, never an exchange call from the browser (`14:2565`). The rate line: `system`'s
`rate_budget_free_pct`, deployment-wide (`23:4331-4332`). The policy period: deployment configuration, read-only
(`D02:630`). The KEK notice: the `system` notice `secrets.kek_unavailable` (`23:4262`) and the server's banner
sentence (`SYS:66`). The card: step 1 is E39's freeze (`POST /trading/kill-switch`; not mounted, `MX:1521-1527`),
step 3 `revokeApiKey` through §7's revoke dialog, step 5 SCR-126's key step (`createApiKey`);
`admin.key_marked_compromised` has no operation and no registered code (G-6; `TM:612`), so the card writes nothing of
its own (`D02:666-671`).

**Keyboard and focus.** Tab: the disclosure → per row, in row order, "Actions for …" → nothing in the policy (it holds
no control). The menu: `Enter`, `Space` or `↓` opens it, `↑` and `↓` move, `Enter` picks, `Esc` closes and returns
focus to its button; a T2 item stays arrow-reachable. Opening the card moves focus to its `h2` (the press moved it);
inside it Tab runs Freeze → the note → Revoke here → Add a new key → Close card, and each step's control opens its own
dialog and returns focus to that control (`D02:686-690`); the steps never time out (A-O). The panel announces
nothing on refresh; a chip's transition goes through the shell announcer once (D21, `D02:1078-1079`). Forced
colours: fills drop; the words and the glyph shapes carry; the card's danger rule and the chips' borders survive as
`CanvasText`; a T2 item's label and lock render `GrayText` and its reason `CanvasText` (BQ-3).

## 7. SCR-129 — Disable, delete and the revoke dialog (board 08)

Three flows on one anatomy: the revoke dialog (E27-S04's; it shares SCR-129's anatomy, `D02:717-718`), Disable, and
Delete (keeps history) — separate flows with different copy (`14:2579`; `D02:713-718`). Each is a CMP-044
alertdialog on E42-D02's ladder (D19, consumed): one rung, the title "{Verb} {object} · {environment}", the
consequences as sentences with counts read before the confirm renders, the exposure choice exactly as the contract
has it, the typed label at rung 3 only, the ask line before the press, the audit marker last, Cancel first
(`D02:260-291`; E42-D03:533-537). The rung props are consumed by name from E42-D03's unlanded CMP-044 proposal —
`rung`, `blastRadius`, `choices` (with `disabledReason`), `stepUpState`, `auditCodes` (E42-D03:902-904) — PROPOSED,
with a "contract pending" stamp on the board until they land (BQ-11). Every confirm here but Enable…'s is the
destructive confirm; each states its consequence before the press and names its step-up (the table below). As on
every admin screen, a Manager, a Viewer and a view-as session meet SCR-155 (T3), so the dialogs' two T2s are state
legs (`D02:1013-1014`).
Comfortable density; board 08 draws frames 49–61 in dark, light by token.

No dialog offers a third choice ("cancel working orders"), pre-selects a choice, renders its confirm before its counts,
or says a disable or a delete closes positions by itself (AD-8, `MEMO:404`; the choices as `22:14501-14515` defines
them). Esc, Cancel and the scrim mean "nothing changed"; no dismissal picks a choice
(E42-D03:556-557).

**Data and producers.** Disable is `updateExchangeAccount` with `enabled: false` (`accounts:write`; `22:2592-2631`,
the disable rule at `22:2601-2606`); delete is `deleteExchangeAccount`, `flatten_first` its only choice
(`22:2632-2669`); revoke is `revokeApiKey` (`keys:manage`; `22:2838-2875`; not mounted, `MX:589-595`), local only —
the key stays valid at Bybit until the Owner deletes it there (`22:2847-2852`). The choices, the stop-loss refusal,
unknown exposure, its remedy and a failed read are defined once at `22:14490-14595`; the `409` bodies are
`22:15092-15188`; the summary is `AccountConsequenceSummary` (`22:16790-16838`), served today only inside the `409`,
so the side-effect-free read before render is E27-S04's to add (G-7; O-D, `D02:1214`). Budget: the summary within
1 s, no confirm until it has loaded (`14:2576`). Events: `api_key.revoke` (registered, `ACT:138`); `account.disabled`
and `account.deleted` have no registered code, so their markers name none (`D02:726-727`), and Enable…'s marker names
none either until D03-Q4 is answered.

**Keyboard and focus (every dialog).** Focus starts on Cancel (`14:2575`). The DOM, and so the Tab cycle, runs as
E42-D03 orders a rung dialog (E42-D03:903, BQ-11): the radio group → the typed field → Cancel → the confirm, then
back to the group (PROPOSED: `D02:765-767` reads the cycle from Cancel, but Cancel stays in the DOM beside the
confirm, where it is drawn). The first Tab from Cancel therefore reaches the confirm, whose `Enter` or `Space`, while
an input is unmet, moves focus to the first unmet input. In the group, Tab enters without selecting, `Space`
selects, the arrows move and select — except that an arrow onto a T2 option focuses it without checking it and
`Space` there re-shows its reason. `Enter` in the group or the typed field never confirms (D22). `Esc` is Cancel. On
close, focus returns to the opener: the row's "Actions for …" button, or the card's "Revoke here…" (`05:97`). The
description is announced once when the consequences are in place; a server refusal is assertive once (CMP-027);
nothing ticks. At 200 % the dialog fills the viewport, its body scrolls and Cancel and the confirm stay one sticky row;
options wrap and never truncate (`D02:1088-1089`). Forced colours: the confirm keeps its 1 px border, and in its
validity look its label renders `GrayText`; a T2 option's label and lock render `GrayText` and its reason
`CanvasText`; the octagon carries the missing stop-loss in `CanvasText` beside its words (E42-D03:642; E42-D05:227;
BQ-3).

## 8. SCR-079 — Account detail drawer, and SCR-019's account tasks (board 09)

The drawer is E27-D02 §5.6 (`D02:770-845`) in colour, and SCR-019's account tasks are E27-D02 §5.7's
(`D02:874-886`) as content. SCR-079 is a CMP-046 modal drawer on the trading shell (SCR-010), outside CMP-087 (D1,
`D02:187`; `D02:175-177`), opened by every role on a granted account from the account picker or the positions grid
(`14:1745`). It keeps its host's density, compact (`16:113`): board 09 draws it compact with one comfortable inset
(BQ-4). What a role sees is what the server serves to it (D15, `D02:201`): the Owner gets the key facts; a Manager and
a Viewer get the key status and health in words, and nothing else of the key (`24:4766`; `D02:806-814`). Every write
in the drawer is gated in the server's leg order, the view-as leg first (T2 per §10.1; the gated set and who sees what
are §10.2). A stale balance keeps full contrast (C-10, `D02:1205`; CD-4, `MEMO:379`). No secret is displayed, ever
(`14:1753`; D13, `D02:199`): the one key value is CMP-034's `...{last4}` (§2.3, BQ-8).

**`detected` stays a badge in the statement list** (§2.1; BQ-6). The Owner's statements are plain text led by their
class glyphs, so a fund right found drawn as one more statement would read like "IP allowlist: no match.", a failed
state; it is the CMP-175 critical badge instead, the list item itself, with its bold word and its 2 px border. No
E27-D02 frame draws a blocked key in the drawer; CMP-175's WithdrawalDetected story carries the form (§13).

**Geometry and density.** Compact rows and controls are 24 px (`size.row.compact`, `size.control.compact`), the
WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 minimum (`16:126`); padding is `space.inset.md`, which the density mode resolves (`themes.json`
`density.resolves`). The comfortable inset draws `SCR-079 / healthy (owner)` once more at 32 px
(`size.row.comfortable`, `size.control.comfortable`); density changes the spacing and nothing else (`16:125`). At
720 CSS px wide or less — 200 % zoom on the 1280 × 800 frame is 640 — the drawer takes the full width and its balance
columns stack (`D02:1089-1090`; §11).

**Light and high contrast.** Every binding above is a token, so the light frame is the same names in
`semantic-light`, and §9 measures every pair in dark, light and high contrast. Two light readings need the shape: the
octagon of a rejected key and the triangle of a rotation due share one hue in light (DS-6; §9 `glyph-critical-warning`
is 0.00 <!-- audit:cvd.glyph-critical-warning.light.normal=0.00 --> there), so the glyph shape and the words carry
them; and the stale chip's clock is 3.37 <!-- audit:pairs.stale-glyph.light=3.37 --> in light (`stale-glyph`), over the
3.0 bar, with its words beside it.

**Data, budget and event** (`D02:796-805`). Every role: `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`balance`,
`balance_stale`, `balance_stale_since`, `health`, `key_status`, the modes, `enabled`), `wallet` and `positions`. The
Owner adds `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`, `GET /admin/security/summary` for the rights and allowlist words —
`not_mounted` at the base (`MX:202-208`), so until it is mounted those statements are the target state, stamped "not
yet served — G-1, #895 / #896" on the board annotation layer (D20, `D02:206`) — and `system`
`exchange.rate_budget_free_pct`. The drawer opens from cached state in ≤ 100 ms and refreshes in place, never a spinner
over cached values (`14:1751`). Event: `account.detail_viewed`, analytics, its payload the viewer's role only (§12.3).

**The hi-fi rows.** Each row draws the anatomy above with the one block it changes; the Board cell is the frame's
board, and the light reading is the same tokens in `semantic-light` (above).

**SCR-019's account tasks, content only** (BQ-1: the card's CMP-097 chrome is E09's; `14:476-486`). The card's two
account tasks are steps of CMP-097's ordered list with read-only checkbox semantics (`aria-checked` reflects
completion), each a CMP-021 link to the screen that completes it (`14:485`): "Register a Bybit account" to SCR-126's
register step and "Add its API key" to SCR-126's key step. The checklist read is self-scoped (`permissions: []`,
`22:12209`), so a view-as session reads the target's set, and every leg is the session's (`D02:878-881`). The Owner's
done line names the key and its verified time, both read from `listApiKeys` (`keys:read`) and never from the
checklist: `OnboardingChecklist.items[]` carries only `key`, `state`, `reason`, `unblock_at` and `action_route`
(`22:21029-21047`) on a read with `permissions: []`, and stays free of key facts, so any other role's done line names
no key fact (D15). Completion is announced politely once (`14:480`).

## 9. Contrast, greyscale and colour vision — the measured matrix

Every number in this section is the output of `docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py` at the base, and each one
carries the marker that `--check` re-derives; none is typed. The tool layers the token JSON as
`packages/ui/tokens/themes.json` does — dark is the primitives plus `semantic-dark`, light adds `semantic-light`, high
contrast adds `semantic-hc` — through `packages/ui/tokens/tests/verify_tokens.py`; it takes every ratio from
`contrast_check.contrast_ratio()` (`docs/design/_tools/contrast_check.py`) and every colour-vision value from
`docs/research/_tools/cvd_simulate.py` (`simulate`, `delta_e76`), imported and never re-implemented (BQ-16). The
commands, run from the repository root:

```text
python3 -I -B docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py             # the report: matrix, CVD and luma, every gate
python3 -I -B docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py --json      # the same numbers as JSON
python3 -I -B docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py --check     # exit 1 on a gated FAIL; re-derives every marker
python3 -I -B docs/design/_tools/e27_d03_hifi_audit.py --self-test # the mutation set and the K list (§16)
```

**Bars.** Text 4.5 and non-text 3.0 in every theme (`05:125-126`); `hc-text` 7.0, gated in high contrast only, for the
critical word, the environment word and dialog body text (`05:127`, `05:130`). `rejected-*`, `decorative` and
`composite` rows are reported and never gated. **Counts.** 62 rows: 57 gated <!-- audit:numbers.pairs_rows=57 -->,
of which 29 are registered in `tools/contrast/pairs.mjs` <!-- audit:numbers.pairs_registered=29 --> and 28 are
PROPOSED for the token owner <!-- audit:numbers.pairs_proposed=28 --> (a design PR never edits `tools/`); 5 are
reported <!-- audit:numbers.pairs_reported=5 -->; 0 FAIL <!-- audit:numbers.pairs_fail=0 -->; 19 rows reproduce a
merged spec's numbers to the hundredth <!-- audit:numbers.repro_rows=19 -->, and 0 of them are
off <!-- audit:numbers.repro_fail=0 -->. A `CR:` row is measured on the token its change request would alias, never
on an invented hex. Pairs a consumed component owns — CMP-003's selected segment, CMP-104's slider, CMP-116's signed
values, CMP-015's skeleton, E42-D02's band and strip — are measured and registered by their owners and are not
re-measured here. SCR-079's two links on the drawer are row 62, `link-overlay`, a pair the registry holds out pending
E47-D03's retune (reading 1 below).

**The focus ring against both neighbours** (ticket a11y notes; `05:99`). CMP-039's ring is `color.focus.ring`,
`border.focus` 2 px wide, at a 2 px offset (`15:423-424`), so both colours it touches are the surface its control sits
on — the gap inside and the field outside. The `ring-*` rows above measure it on every surface and fill an E27 control
sits on; the lowest is the warning fill in dark, 4.57 <!-- audit:pairs.ring-warning.dark=4.57 -->, and every value is
over 3.0 in every theme. Over CMP-039's seven tiers (app, canvas, raised, overlay, hover, selected, sunken) the minima
reproduce E05-D02's: dark 4.72 <!-- audit:ring_min.dark=4.72 -->, light 4.81 <!-- audit:ring_min.light=4.81 -->,
high contrast 12.26 <!-- audit:ring_min.high-contrast=12.26 -->. A ring never sits on its own control's fill — the
offset keeps it on the surface around the control — and in forced colours it is `Highlight` (below).

**E30-D02's dimmed validity look** (composite; reported, never gated): the label of an unmet primary confirm at
`opacity.disabled` 0.45 <!-- audit:numbers.opacity_disabled=0.45 --> over its own dimmed fill on a dialog measures
dark 3.30 <!-- audit:composite.dark=3.30 -->, light 1.46 <!-- audit:composite.light=1.46 --> and high contrast 1.72 <!-- audit:composite.high-contrast=1.72 -->.
That is why no E27 frame draws it: CMP-044's unmet confirm takes E42-D03's validity form instead (§2.4, §10.3; BQ-11)
— its fill `color.surface.raised` with a `color.border.default` hairline and its label `color.text.tertiary`, the
`t2-label` pair — and its hint sentence in full-opacity `color.text.secondary` carries the meaning; the T2 binding
never dims (`t2-dimmed`, rejected).

**Reported, not gated — two readings for the token owner.** (1) `color.text.link` has no high-contrast override
(`semantic-hc.tokens.json` overrides 14 tokens <!-- audit:numbers.token_files.hc=14 -->, the link not among them): a
link on the row measures 6.66 <!-- audit:pairs.row-link.high-contrast=6.66 --> in high contrast, over the 4.5 text bar
this matrix gates and under the 7:1 body-text aim of the high-contrast theme (`05:130`); its dialog and drawer twin,
`link-overlay` (row 62), measures 6.15 <!-- audit:pairs.link-overlay.high-contrast=6.15 --> there, the "6.15:1 in
HC" <!-- audit:pairs.link-overlay.high-contrast=6.15 --> the registry holds out (`tools/contrast/pairs.mjs:193`). CMP-021 underlines every link (`15:247`), so no link
depends on its colour; the retune is the token owner's, routed as D03-H7 (§14). (2) The closest
gated values to a bar are light glyphs: CMP-066's done check on a dialog, 3.11 <!-- audit:pairs.step-done.light=3.11 -->,
and the pass check on its fill, 3.34 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-pass-glyph.light=3.34 -->; both pass, and both sit beside
their words.

the carriers in §2.1 instead — a word of its own, the glyph of its severity class, and the critical state's bold word
and 2 px border (BQ-6) — and reports Delta E76 (CIE76) under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia against the 5.0

What the rows say, and what carries each collapse instead of colour:

- **Critical and failed glyphs against the warning glyphs, in light:** 0.00 <!-- audit:cvd.glyph-critical-warning.light.normal=0.00 -->
  under every simulation — `color.status.danger.strong` is `color.status.warning.strong` in light (DS-6) — so the
  octagon against the triangle and clock, and the words, carry it on boards 02 and 05, and BLOCKED adds its bold word
  and 2 px border.
- **The critical fill against the pass fill under deuteranopia:** dark 4.46 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-critical-pass.dark.deuteranopia=4.46 -->, light 1.05 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-critical-pass.light.deuteranopia=1.05 -->.
  The subtle fills are never the carrier: "BLOCKED — fund right found", the octagon, the bold and the border are.
- **The failed fill against the warning fill under tritanopia, in dark:** 4.45 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-critical-warning.dark.tritanopia=4.45 -->;
  the octagon against the triangle, and the words, carry it.
- **The stored read-only info glyph against the pass check under tritanopia, in dark:** 1.34 <!-- audit:cvd.glyph-info-pass.dark.tritanopia=1.34 -->;
  the info and check shapes differ, and the read-only state exists at component level only (BQ-5's rider).
- **The not-checked fill in light:** against the pass fill under tritanopia 4.81 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-unknown-pass.light.tritanopia=4.81 -->,
  against the critical fill under protanopia 3.15 <!-- audit:cvd.fill-unknown-critical.light.protanopia=3.15 -->; the
  dash and "Withdrawal: not checked" carry it, and it never reads as a pass (AD-2).
- **A solid danger fill against the LIVE accent, in high contrast:** 5.14 <!-- audit:cvd.solid-danger-live.high-contrast.normal=5.14 -->,
  and 2.56 under protanopia <!-- audit:cvd.solid-danger-live.high-contrast.protanopia=2.56 -->, beside its
  rejected 4.54 <!-- audit:pairs.c175-solid-danger.high-contrast=4.54 --> as hc text: BQ-6's alternative (a) stays
  rejected, never drawn.
- **DEMO against LIVE:** at least 91.86 <!-- audit:cvd.env-demo-live.dark.protanopia=91.86 --> in every theme and
  simulation — distinct, and the words carry it anyway (`14:81`).

## 10. T2 — the rule stated once, the gated set and what is not T2

### 10.1 The T2 rule (stated once)

Every control that a view-as context, a permission, a grant, the environment or a known state blocks is E09-D09's T2
(`14:85` rule 5; E09-D09 §2.1–§2.2, `D09:32-49`; §9.1–§9.3, `D09:224-246`; GATE G-T2.1a–G-T2.6, `GATE:17-61`), in
every frame and state row that shows one, and each such row cites this paragraph as "T2 per §10.1". **Legs, in the
server's order** (E09-D09 §2.1; `22:281-290`): the view-as leg first on every write — `rbac.view_as`, "Read-only while
viewing as {user}." — because the server refuses `view_as_read_only` before it authorises; then the permission or
owner-only leg (`rbac.permission`, `rbac.owner_only`, each with its {verb} from E09-D09 §3.2), then the grant
(`rbac.account_read_only`), then the environment (`rbac.env`), and last a registered state — the ten PROPOSED E27 keys
of §12.2 (vocabulary owner E27, registration routed by C-9, `D02:1204`) and E30-D02 §14's `frozen`, `lockout` and
`arm.locked`, consumed; the first leg that holds gives the reason. Admin controls have no role leg, because only the
Owner reaches `/admin/accounts` (T3 for everyone else, `D02:166-171`), so their T2s are state legs; none of E27's gated
controls is a C-2.6 protective write, so the view-as carve-out (`D09:95`) names no control here (GATE R5).
**Semantics:** the control keeps its native role and its full label; `aria-disabled="true"`, never the `disabled`
attribute, so it stays in the Tab order and a menu item stays arrow-reachable; the reason node is in the DOM at mount
and linked by `aria-describedby`; where one state blocks a whole panel or drawer, one notice carries the reason and
every gated control points at it — one notice, many pointers (the KEK notice of BQ-9, SCR-079's key-rejected,
disabled, no-key and view-as notices). **Rendering:** every E27 T2 is 2a inline — under or beside the control, a menu
item's or a checklist step's second line, a radio's description; none needs the 2b tooltip echo or the sentence form.
**Components:** CMP-079 RbacGate wraps every gated control (`form="notice"` with its `noticeId` where one notice serves
many); a CMP-019 `lock` glyph (`decorative=false`, accessible name "Not available") leads the label. **Visual, in every
theme and density:** the label and the lock in `color.text.tertiary` and the reason in `color.text.secondary`, measured
in §9 (`t2-label`, `t2-label-page`, `dialog-tertiary`; `row-secondary`, `dialog-secondary`); the enabled fill goes, so
a filled control — primary, secondary or a selected segment — takes `color.surface.raised` with a
`color.border.default` hairline, and a selected segment keeps its selection as a check glyph and `aria-checked`; never
`color.text.disabled` and never `opacity.disabled`, whose 2.86 <!-- audit:pairs.t2-dimmed.dark=2.86 --> in dark is the rejected `t2-dimmed` row. **Keys:**
`Enter`, `Space`, a bound hotkey or an arrow onto a T2 radio changes nothing and re-shows the reason inline with one
polite announcement; `↑` and `↓` land on a T2 menu item without activating it (E09-D09 §9.3). **Nothing else:** a T2
control emits no audit record and no analytics event; the host decides every leg, and an atom renders only the
`disabledReason` it is given (E09-D09 §8); the UI is never the control — the server refuses and audits regardless
(C-2.12, C-12.4).

### 10.3 What is NOT T2

Over-converting is as wrong as under-converting (E09-D09 §2.1; `D02:1027-1039`). None of these draws a lock, takes
CMP-079 or names a reason key:

- **Busy** — Verify and save, Run test and Verify and switch while their own request runs: CMP-001's `loading` with
  `aria-busy="true"`, focusable, the validating copy beside it (D18); a key in its overlap, "Rotation in progress · old
  key usable until {hh:mm:ss} UTC" (`e27.scr125.busy.overlap`).
- **Outcome** — an action done or no longer applicable shows its outcome line instead (#960 Q13): an import on an
  account with an active key is the key row with Rotate (AD-1); "Revoked at {hh:mm} UTC — delete it at Bybit"; "Disabled
  at {hh:mm} UTC — doesn't trade here." with Enable…; a passed Test's result line; stage 5's done line.
- **Availability** — what the contract does not serve yet is drawn as "not yet served — {gap}, {owner}" on the board
  annotation layer, never as a control (D20): rollback, early revoke, the drain read and a failed rotation (G-4), the
  trading re-arm (G-12), a compromise operation (G-6), a policy write, the KEK status (O-H), and the egress-IP read
  before any check (BQ-15 item 7; D03-G1).
- **The validity look** — form validity, E42-D03's form for a rung confirm (`E42-D03:542`, `E42-D03:566-567`),
  adopted for CMP-044 by BQ-11 in place of E30-D02's dimmed look (`E30-D02:128`): a rung-3 confirm before the
  summary has loaded is not rendered at all (Cancel only); after it, until the typed label matches and, where there
  are two, a radio is chosen, the confirm stays focusable with `aria-disabled`, its danger fill dropped to
  `color.surface.raised` with a `color.border.default` hairline, its label `color.text.tertiary` and its hint in
  full-opacity `color.text.secondary` under it — no lock, no CMP-079, no key (layer `validity-reason`); empty key fields show an
  inline error on press (CMP-040).
- **T4** — a server refusal at the point of action, then the control re-derives its legs: `409 conflict`, `412`,
  `422`, `429` ("Tested at {hh:mm:ss} UTC; the next test can run at {hh:mm:ss} UTC."), `409 open_exposure` and
  `exposure_unknown`, `403 kek_unavailable` after a stale view, `view_as_read_only` (recorded
  `admin.view_as_refused`), and `trading_disabled` with `account_disabled_by_policy` (E30-D02's refusal).
- **T1** — a missing step-up: the control stays enabled, its ask line says what the press will ask, and the press
  opens SCR-006 (E09-D06's, consumed); nothing is locked for want of elevation (`14:85`).
- **T3** — every admin route for a Manager, a Viewer and a view-as session (SCR-155, identical to any unknown route),
  and SCR-079's two bare links for every role but the Owner: hidden, never locked (`14:85` step 1; `D02:809-812`).

A sticky header or footer leaves scroll padding equal to its height, so a focused control is never hidden under it
(`05:99`, WCAG 2.4.11).

**Targets and the ring.** The admin screens are comfortable: 32 px controls (`size.control.comfortable`), never under
24 px (`size.target.min`; `16:127`; `05:100`). SCR-079 is compact: 24 px controls, exactly the WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 minimum
(`16:126`), and 32 px in the comfortable inset. The Bybit note checkbox and each radio take a hit area of at least
24 × 24 px with their label. The ring is CMP-039's everywhere — 2 px at a 2 px offset, measured against both of its
neighbours on every E27 surface and fill in §9 — and `Highlight` in forced colours.

**Forced colours** (R2): per carrier in §9's table; board 10's strip draws them.

The countdown never speaks per tick, the health chips never speak on a refresh, and a T2 control never speaks on its
own: the only voice it has is the reason, re-shown on a keystroke.

## 12. Copy deck — keyed, validated against E27-D01

### 12.1 The deck

Every product string the eight screens, the cross-screen patterns and the contributed components show, keyed so that a
screen cites a key and never writes its own string (the ticket's Technical notes; BQ-15). **Ids** are
`e27.{screen}.{element}[.{state}]`; the screen segment is `shell` (the accounts route's chrome), `scr125` to `scr129`,
`scr079`, `scr016` and `scr019`, `checks` (the check list of frame 3, reused on SCR-126, SCR-127, the Test dialog and
SCR-016), `cmp034` and `cmp175` (the components' own strings), or `shared` (a line several screens show). **Where**
names the surface, the element and E27-D02's frame numbers. **Status · source:** `unchanged` is byte-equal to the
E27-D01 memo's CD-n or CP-n seed (`MEMO:358-383`), which the tool checks; `refined` names its seed or source and the
change; `new` is this spec's, PROPOSED for the owner; `consumed` is verbatim in the merged file it names, which the tool
checks — E27-D02's own strings are PROPOSED there and stay so, and a server's sentence is never rewritten. `{…}` are
fills; every time reads UTC (`D02:178`); a key id is `...` plus 4 (D13). The tool's copy gate holds every string here:
no "reveal", "irreversible", "permanently", "step-up", "re-authentication", "Bybit says" or "n/a"; "expiry" only with
Bybit's name (AD-5); every clock time followed by UTC, or "left" for a duration; a withdrawal "OFF" or "off" only
beside its verified time (AD-3); no withdrawal or transfer right drawn as allowed. Where E27-D02 wrote a string
across a line break, the deck unwraps it (`refined`, words unchanged); where it wrote a fixture value, the deck writes
the fill.

Rows: 327 <!-- audit:numbers.deck_rows=327 --> — unchanged 10 <!-- audit:numbers.deck_by_status.unchanged=10 -->,
refined 124 <!-- audit:numbers.deck_by_status.refined=124 -->, new 66 <!-- audit:numbers.deck_by_status.new=66 -->,
consumed 127 <!-- audit:numbers.deck_by_status.consumed=127 -->. The ticket's six required items are marked
**required** in Where: the withdrawal verdict (`e27.scr125.verdict.*`, `e27.cmp175.withdrawal_detected`,
`e27.scr125.blocked.line2`, the import refusal `e27.scr126.refused.withdrawal`, the onboarding result row
`e27.scr016.result`, the drawer's statements); the IP-mismatch remediation with the allowlist set in Bybit's dashboard
(CD-3's two forms, CP-3 at the allowlist row and stage 1, `e27.scr079.ip_mismatch`, `e27.scr129.unknown.fixable`,
policy 4); the stale-balance badge (`e27.scr079.stale` and its CD-4 suffix); the irreversible-delete warning, met
without that word (`e27.scr129.delete.history`, BQ-15 item 8); revoke and leave positions versus flatten first
(`e27.scr129.choice.*` and the confirm labels); and the write-only secret explanation (CP-1 on every secret field,
`e27.scr126.edit.write_only`, `e27.scr128.policy.write_only`, `e27.cmp034.description`).

### 12.2 T2 reason keys

A screen never writes its own reason (GATE G-T2.4): every gated control in §10.2 names one of these keys. The ten E27
keys are PROPOSED, vocabulary owner E27, their registration beside E30-D02's state vocabulary routed to E09-D09 §3.1 by
C-9 (`D02:1204`); each is one sentence of at most 60 characters with a full stop, naming a capability, never data
(`D09:402`). The `rbac.*` rows are E09-D09 §3.1's strings, verbatim, with the {verb} each control fills from E09-D09
§3.2. Reason keys: 15 <!-- audit:numbers.reason_keys=15 -->, of them E27's 10 <!-- audit:numbers.reason_keys_e27=10 -->.

### 12.3 Observability

No runtime telemetry is added (the ticket's Observability): each frame carries the audit or analytics annotation
E27-D02 gave it (`D02:922-999`), on the board annotation layer and as the product's audit marker where one is shown. A
marker names a registered code or none: with no registered code it reads "Recorded in the audit log"
(`e27.scr129.marker`; E42-D02 D5), and a frame never names a code the registry lacks (`D02:727`). Payloads carry
fingerprints or ids, never key material (`TM:597`; `D02:476-477`, `D02:563`); an idempotency fingerprint leaves out
`api_key` and `api_secret` or is a keyed hash (SR-E27-20, `TM:673`); and `account.detail_viewed` carries only the
viewer's role (`D02:805`). **A T2 control emits nothing.**

### 12.4 Validation against E27-D01

Nothing here is measured: no E27-D01 session has run (`MEMO:350-356`; `PROT:6-8`), and no participant, score, timing or
quote is invented. Under the ticket's adaptation, "copy re-tested for comprehension with at least two people who were
not in the E27-D01 sessions" is three things: the heuristic re-test below `(heuristic)`, the written protocol after it
for the owner to run with two such people, and the owner-walkthrough items of §15. The pass rule stays the memo's: "any
statement misunderstood by more than one participant is rewritten and retested" (`MEMO:355-356`). H6's predicted
misreads (CP-2, CP-4, CP-6; `MEMO:194`) are not rewritten without a measurement; their placement is what this spec
strengthens (BQ-15 item 3).

**The heuristic re-test, probe by probe** (`MEMO:360-365`; every row `(heuristic)`):

| Probe (the fact)                                 | Deck keys carrying it                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | H6's prediction          | What the placement does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

| CP-1 — the secret can never be shown again       | `e27.scr126.secret.help`, `e27.scr127.secret.help` (byte-equal to CP-1, also SCR-016 step 3's); `e27.scr126.edit.write_only`, `e27.scr128.policy.write_only`, `e27.scr126.saved`, `e27.cmp034.description`                                     | restated correctly       | the sentence is each secret field's description at mount; no control near it resembles a reveal (CMP-034 and CMP-201 write-only, BQ-8); no ask line suggests that a code unlocks anything, the misreading CP-1 names                                                         |
| CP-2 — a backup without the KEK is useless       | `e27.scr128.policy.backups` (byte-equal); `e27.scr129.delete.bybit`                                                                                                                                                                            | misread by more than one | both places carry both clauses; the delete dialog states it where a delete makes it matter; the wording waits for a measurement                                                                                                                                              |
| CP-3 — the allowlist is set in Bybit's dashboard | `e27.scr126.allowlist.help`, `e27.scr127.stage1.allowlist`, `e27.scr126.refused.ip_bybit`, `e27.scr126.refused.ip_rule`, `e27.scr125.details.allowlist`, `e27.scr079.ip_mismatch`, `e27.scr129.unknown.fixable`, `e27.scr128.policy.allowlist` | restated correctly       | every form says who refused, the one address, "exactly" or "and nothing else", and "in Bybit's dashboard"; it is a read-only row with one [Copy], never an input; before any check the address is a target state, never an echo (BQ-15 item 7)                               |
| CP-4 — revoked here, still valid at Bybit        | `e27.scr127.stage5.revoked`, `e27.scr129.revoked.row` (byte-equal); `e27.scr129.revoke.not_last`, `e27.scr129.delete.bybit`, `e27.shell.notice.deleted`, `e27.scr125.outcome.revoked`                                                          | misread by more than one | both clauses always appear together; the overlap's end announces CP-4 itself (§11); the one Bybit note follows it and gates, unlocks and records nothing (`e27.shared.bybit_note`)                                                                                           |
| CP-5 — a key that can withdraw is never stored   | `e27.scr126.refused.withdrawal` (byte-equal; SCR-016 step 3's too)                                                                                                                                                                             | not predicted            | "Nothing was stored." leads the refusal and both fields clear at once; on a stored key the same fact is the BLOCKED row with the compromise response first, never Rotate                                                                                                     |
| CP-6 — a Test enforces its verdict               | `e27.scr125.test.before`, `e27.scr125.test.passed_read_only` (byte-equal); `e27.scr128.test_note`                                                                                                                                              | misread by more than one | the before-sentence is the Test dialog's description, read before Run test; the failed verdict (CD-2) says the same "until a restart passes the check" and takes E30-D02's "disabled by policy", so the line and the order ticket's refusal read as one story (BQ-15 item 4) |

**H7 — every "delete" and "revoke" names where it happens** (`MEMO:195`). A scan of the deck for the two verbs finds
each string that does not name its place itself, and the line read with it that does: the menu item "Revoke key…" and
the revoke title open a dialog whose first consequence says "here" and "at Bybit" (`e27.scr129.revoke.not_last`,
`e27.scr129.revoke.last`); the compromise card's "the revoke" lines sit under step 3, "Revoke it here — ends the key in
CandleViewer."; "Not revoked: …" points at once to step 2 (`e27.scr128.card.refused.next`); the delete confirms sit
under the title "Delete {label} (keeps history) · {ENV}" and CD-5's lines, which end with "Its keys still work at Bybit
until you delete them there."; "The account's API key was revoked." is the server's own text (`REV:108`), never
rewritten. Every new revoke label names the place in its own words (`e27.scr129.revoke.confirm`,
`e27.scr129.revoke.confirm_leave`, `e27.scr129.revoke.confirm_flatten`).

**CD-2 aligned with E30-D02** (`MEMO:377`; BQ-15 item 4). The failed verdict's account clause now says "order entry on
that key's account stays disabled by policy until it is turned back on", the words of E30-D02's
`refusal.trading_disabled.account_disabled_by_policy` ("Order entry is disabled on {account} by policy",
`E30-D02:437`). The verdict says "that key's account", not "{account}", because the stored-key notice names no key and
no account (`23:4270-4271`) — D03-Q1, to the orchestrator (§14).

**The written protocol for two people outside the E27-D01 sessions** (ready for the owner; never run by an agent):

1. **Who.** Two people the owner names who took part in no E27-D01 session (`PROT:17-27`); fewer than two leaves the
   ticket's test-plan row open with the number that ran. An agent may read the prompts aloud and receives no answer.
2. **Consent and data.** E27-D01's opening and consent scripts and data rules, verbatim (`PROT:29-67`): fixture values
   only (`PROT:44-46`); nothing connected; recordings and notes on the owner's encrypted host, never in the repository,
   Penpot, GitHub, RelayRoom, a chat or an AI tool.
3. **Material.** The boards of this spec, or the deck strings on cards, each card labelled with its key.
4. **Probes.** For CP-1 to CP-6, in the memo's method (`PROT:111-119`): show the string for 10 s, remove it, ask the
   memo's restate prompt (`MEMO:360-365`), record the restatement verbatim and score it understood, partially
   understood or misunderstood against the memo's "understood if" column; then show the CD seed that carries the same
   fact and ask "What would you do next?". Participant A sees CP-1 to CP-6 in order, participant B in reverse (H5
   counterbalancing, `MEMO:193`).
5. **H7 prompts.** For each of the six required items, after the string is removed: "Where does this happen — here, or
   in Bybit's dashboard?", scored by the same three words.
6. **Two added prompts** (PROPOSED). The compromise card (`e27.scr128.card.*`): "You suspect sub_001's key leaked.
   What do you do first, second and third?" — understood if: freeze here, delete the key in Bybit's dashboard at once,
   then revoke it here (W3, `MEMO:510-513`). Activation failed (`e27.scr126.activation_failed`): "Where is this key
   now?" — understood if: stored revoked here, and still working at Bybit.
7. **Pass rule and the record.** A string misunderstood by both people is rewritten and retested in the next session; a
   misread by one is a signal (`PROT:132-151`). Findings go into the memo as a dated addendum (`PROT:153-165`), never a
   new document; a deck row moves from `unchanged` to `refined` only on a measured finding.

Heuristic only: Nielsen's N1–N10 and `05`'s trading readings A-P, A-O and A-U, as the memo numbers them (`MEMO:24`,
`MEMO:135-137`). No participant, session or timing exists, and none is invented: AC3's fresh reviewer and the
ticket's two people are the walkthrough below and §12.4's protocol, both the owner's to run. Severity: **critical** —
a misreading moves money, strands a position or hides a fund right; **major** — a wrong step or a lost minute;
**minor** — friction.

**Security record** (the conditions main-orchestrator bound on 2026-10-24, at 12:53Z and in the 14:22Z ruling). (1)
Metadata only: a key appears as its label, `...{last4}`, its rights, environment, status and dates, the Owner's alone
(C-12.2; §2.3, §8). (2) No key material, no plaintext and no reveal: CMP-034 is text only and CMP-201 write-only, and
no frame draws more than the masked id (BQ-8; C-2.7). (3) Withdrawal is never drawn as allowed: a fund right is CP-5's
refusal on import and BLOCKED on a stored key, and the copy gate refuses any string that grants it (C-2.8; §16). (4)
Revoke, disable, delete and rotate are confirmable, each stating its consequence before the press (§5, §7; the
destructive-confirms table). (5) T2 is E09-D09's, the view-as leg first (§10.1). (6) E27-D02 is cited by its text and
line, never by a board id.
